extracted.intended_audience: general TED audience; people interested in Twitter/online trust-and-safety
extracted.subtask_description: A short TED Talk (Del Harvey, TED2014) describing Twitter's Trust and Safety team's work to prevent abuse, trolling, and stalking while preserving users' ability to speak. The page is a video landing/summary for a public-audience talk about online safety at scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent worst-case scenarios (abuse, trolling, stalking)
rubrics_metrics.description: prevent worst-case scenarios -- abuse, trolling, stalking
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the page: 'Del Harvey heads up Twitter’s Trust and Safety Team, and she thinks all day about how to prevent worst-case scenarios -- abuse, trolling, stalking.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Give voice to people around the globe
rubrics_metrics.description: giving voice to people around the globe
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page emphasizes balancing safety measures with allowing global users to 'give voice'—i.e., preserving expression while reducing harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operate at scale (keep 240 million users safe)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The talk is framed around how the Trust and Safety team works to protect a very large user base: 'how she works to keep 240 million users safe.' This implies scalability and systems-level considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance safety and speech (Trust & Safety tradeoffs)
rubrics_metrics.description: preventing worst-case scenarios while giving voice to people
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit criterion in the page: the Trust and Safety role requires balancing protection from abuse with preserving users' voices ('...prevent worst-case scenarios ... while giving voice to people around the globe').
